headline: Power-hungry AI boom lifts output but breaks the white-collar ladder and grid

events: Spring capability jump: agentic models reliably complete multi-day software, legal and accounting workflows; enterprise agent seats triple
Hyperscaler capex passes $900bn annualised; US data-centre load growth forces PJM and ERCOT emergency capacity auctions, wholesale power prices up ~40%
US-China agree a quiet tariff truce extension; chip export controls stay but trade volumes stabilise
Entry-level hiring in finance, BPO and customer service falls ~30%; India and Philippines call-centre layoffs begin
Fed cuts once to 3.25% then pauses as electricity and services inflation stick near 3.5%
Second jump: computer-use agents displace back-office, paralegal, junior coding and claims-processing roles at scale; US unemployment rises to 6.1%
G20 inflation peaks at 4.6% as energy, copper and transformer shortages collide with strong capex demand
US election dominated by 'robots and rent'; winning platform promises an AI windfall tax and wage insurance
Gas-turbine and small-reactor orders surge; several US states pause data-centre permits after summer brownouts
Egypt and Pakistan enter IMF-backed restructurings as outsourcing remittances and dollar funding dry up
AI equity correction: leading AI stocks fall ~35% on margin compression as open-weight models commoditise inference; brief credit wobble in data-centre private credit
Global unemployment peaks at 6.9%; youth unemployment above 25% across South Asia and North Africa
US passes Transition Security Act: wage insurance, expanded EITC and a 2% levy on large-model compute revenue; deficit widens to 7.5% of GDP
EU adopts 'human-in-the-loop' rules for public services and a Europe-wide retraining fund financed by joint debt
Kenya and Bangladesh see mass protests over vanishing digital-services jobs; Bangladesh government falls
Third jump: robotics foundation models reach warehouses, logistics and fast food; blue-collar automation spreads in US, China and Korea
Productivity growth in US and China runs above 3%, disinflation in goods and services brings G20 inflation to ~2.6%; central banks cut toward 2.75%
China uses AI-driven manufacturing to push export surplus higher; EU and Mexico impose targeted safeguard duties but no broad trade war
Long-running Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions erupt into open war over Red Sea access
Solar plus battery buildout accelerates as hyperscalers sign record PPAs; coal retirements slow in Asia due to load growth
Unemployment eases to 6.2% as care, construction, energy and AI-supervision jobs absorb part of displaced workers, at lower average wages
Labour share of GDP in OECD falls to a post-war low; top 1% wealth share hits record
Ghana and Sri Lanka slip back into debt distress; G20 launches an AI-linked debt-swap facility
Several countries pilot four-day weeks and 'compute dividends'; US debates a universal basic stipend
Global emissions edge up slightly versus plateau as data-centre gas demand offsets renewables gains

winners: Frontier AI labs, chipmakers and grid/energy equipment suppliers
Owners of capital and land near power and fibre
Skilled trades, electricians and care workers
US and China as AI-productivity hubs
Countries with cheap clean power and spare grid capacity (Nordics, Gulf, Quebec)
losers: Entry-level white-collar workers and recent graduates
Outsourcing economies (India BPO, Philippines, Kenya, Egypt)
Fiscally stretched sovereigns in the Global South
bullets: Global output grew a strong ~3.6% a year, but gains accrued mainly to capital; labour share and wage growth for median workers lagged badly.
Around 175 million jobs were displaced cumulatively, with the junior rungs of professional careers hollowed out and graduate underemployment endemic.
Data centres consume roughly 6% of world electricity; power prices, not chips, became the binding constraint and a hot political issue.
Inflation spiked to 4.6% in 2028 on energy and materials bottlenecks, then AI-driven productivity delivered a disinflationary second half.
Public debt rose to ~101% of world GDP as governments funded wage insurance, retraining and stimulus; US debt reached ~131%.
Trade tensions stayed contained, though AI-boosted Chinese exports triggered targeted safeguards rather than a broad war.
Unrest concentrated in youth-heavy outsourcing economies; one government fell and four sovereigns hit debt crises.
Trust in institutions slid further as voters saw tech fortunes boom while entry-level jobs disappeared.
wildcard: A 2029 autonomous-agent trading cascade briefly froze US Treasury futures markets for 40 minutes, prompting emergency circuit-breaker rules for AI agents in finance.
image_description: In a humid Manila evening in 2031, former call-centre workers queue outside a converted mall for a government retraining session in solar installation, while the glowing data centre across the bay hums under the flicker of rationed streetlights.
